The layoffs at Whirlpool’s Amana, Iowa facility, announced on April 1, 2025, were primarily due to reduced consumer demand for refrigeration products manufactured at the plant. Whirlpool Corporation stated that the workforce reduction of approximately 651 employees, effective June 1, 2025, was a necessary adjustment to align production with current market conditions. The company emphasized that the layoffs were not related to tariffs but were driven by a decline in demand for specific appliances, particularly refrigerators, produced at the Amana facility. This facility, which employs around 2,000 workers, assembles refrigeration products under brands like Amana, JennAir, KitchenAid, Maytag, and Whirlpool. The decision followed a broader trend of job losses in Iowa’s manufacturing sector, which shed 7,600 jobs over the past year, with 5,600 in durable goods like appliances. Whirlpool also noted a projected sales drop to $15.8 billion in 2025 from $17 billion in 2024 and $19 billion in 2023, reflecting challenging market conditions. However, on April 28, 2025, Whirlpool announced a delay of these layoffs until later in the year, without specifying a new timeline.
The largest layoff was in Amana, Iowa, when 651 workers were laid off from refrigerator manufacturer Whirlpool.
